name: Carvin & Ivan — neo-soul half (Carvin Haggins & Ivan Barias)
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 neo-soul — Carvin & Ivan — neo-soul half (Carvin Haggins & Ivan Barias)
notes: **A deliberate split entry.** The volume states that "only the neo-soul half of this duo is claimed here — `rnb-2000s` holds the entry covering their radio-R&B placements", and that the separately-listed Ivan Barias credit is folded in here rather than given a third record of the same people. The id carries the split so it can never collide with the `rnb-2000s` model of the same duo; this file covers the **Musiq Soulchild and Jill Scott axis, 2000–2010** only. The band is the entry's 71–110 straight on 2&4. Drums are the A Touch of Jazz lineage: "a **live-feel, lightly-swung kit over a programmed base**, backbeat on 2&4, played hat/ride, continuous hand percussion. They came up as solo hip-hop artists before producing, which is why the grid stays hip-hop under soul harmony." Lightly-swung is `swing.amount` 0.6, below the parent's 0.63; the programmed base is `quantizeStrength` 0.72; and "continuous hand percussion" is a five-lane percussion set at 4–7 hits a bar including the played ride. Harmony is "Philadelphia-soul with real cadences — 4-chord cycles with 7ths, 9ths and passing chords rather than 2-chord vamps", so `maxChords` stays at 4, the extension spread is seventh-and-ninth led, `susOrDimProb` carries the passing chords, and the harmonic rhythm moves every bar. The keys are the ones the entry names in the Musiq catalogue. Bass is "played bass with walking motion rather than a sustained 808; light sub-doubling on the singles" — no `bass808` block, since a doubling sub is not a replacement. "They work as producers-plus-engineers… which is why their records have a consistent chord-rich live bed", and they produce whole songs, which is the full arrangement rather than a loop. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum number and all melody figures; the research marks the parametric detail as Philadelphia-lane inference.
